title: How accurately a chart can be read — Image Wiki

rules.rule: If comparing values via ink properties like length or angle, assume the reader will consistently underestimate differences and rank them lower than position-based charts.
rules.evidence: The failure is not just noisier, it is biased in a known direction: for true percentages between 25 and 50, Cleveland and McGill's subjects consistently underestimated length and angle differences (p. 544).

rules.rule: If comparing values via colour saturation or shading, assume the reader will conflate light/dark mass with quantity rather than reading an unambiguous magnitude order.
rules.evidence: Colour hue and texture were left off deliberately: they have no unambiguous small-to-large order, which makes them good for naming categories and bad for carrying quantities (p. 532).
